record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.context_brief: Schur-positivity for symmetric real stable polynomials
record.original_question:
Let p be a symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomial of degree d
in n variables with d ≤ n, and suppose p has at
least one positive coefficient in the monomial basis, hence all
monomial coefficients are nonnegative. When p is
expanded in the Schur basis as p(z1, ..., zn) = Σ_{λ ⊢ d} a_λ s_λ(z1,
..., zn), is every coefficient a_λ nonnegative,
i.e. is p Schur-positive?

evidence.quote: Problem 36 ([14]). Let p be a symmetric, real stable and homogeneous polynomial of degree d in n variables with d ≤ n and suppose that p has at least one positive (and then all non-negative) coefficients in the monomial basis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polynomial p ∈ ℝ[z_1,…,z_n] is called real stable if p has real coefficients and p(z_1,…,z_n) ≠ 0 whenever Im(z_j) > 0 for every j = 1,…,n. Let p be a symmetric (invariant under all permutations of the variables), real stable, and homogeneous polynomial of degree d in n variables, with d ≤ n. Assume that p has at least one positive coefficient when expanded in the monomial basis (it is known that under these hypotheses this forces all monomial coefficients of p to be nonnegative). Expand p in the basis of Schur polynomials:
  p(z_1,…,z_n) = Σ_{λ ⊢ d} a_λ · s_λ(z_1,…,z_n),
where the sum ranges over partitions λ of d with at most n parts, and s_λ denotes the Schur polynomial associated with λ.

Question: Must every coefficient a_λ be nonnegative? Equivalently, is every such polynomial p Schur-positive?
artifact.category_tag: Real stable polynomials and Schur positivity
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem on the AIM workshop problem list on Pólya–Schur–Lax problems. Searches for "symmetric real stable polynomial Schur positive" turn up no resolution of this conjecture; related work explores characterizations of symmetric real stable polynomials and Schur-positive log-concavity, but no proof or counterexample to the Schur-positivity question for symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomials with d ≤ n appears in the literature.
